title: fix(objectql)!: an after* hook carrying a condition rolls its write back when the condition cannot be evaluated
body:
Fixes #22856
Clause-②: no (narrowing)

## What the caller sees

A hook `condition` that cannot be evaluated aborts the operation whatever the hook's `onError` says. The gate throws `HookConditionError` outside `onError`, and before an `async: true` hook detaches. Until now the write door opened its unit of work only for a blocking `onError: 'abort'` hook. So an `after*` hook with `onError: 'log'` or `async: true` whose condition could not be evaluated refused the caller while the row stayed stored. The card measured this on REST `createData`: `500`, and the row was stored.

Now the refused write leaves no row behind. The row and the hook chain's engine writes roll back together. The refusal itself is unchanged: the same `500`.

This is declared a narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `minor`, BREAKING). Inside the new unit the rules of any unit apply. On an object carrying such a hook, a blocking `onError: 'log'` hook's write to an object on another datasource is refused with `CrossDatasourceTransactionWriteError` and logged where it used to land. So is such a write made by the part of an `async: true` body that runs before the unit's callback settles. A MongoDB default store without a replica set refuses writes to those objects. The changeset gives the fix: drop the `condition`, keep the objects on one datasource, or run MongoDB as a replica set.

## What changed

- `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`, `opensAfterAbortUnit`. The predicate also counts a metadata-bound `after*` hook that carries a `condition`, whatever its `onError` and `async`. This is triage 6110316957's direction. The first line (the closed-handle reading that PR #22894 landed) stays as it is, and so do the `skipAutomations` exit and the off-default-driver and no-transactions exits. The `DISPATCHABLE_HOOK_EVENTS` docblock now lists the new case.
- `packages/objectql/src/hook-wrappers.ts`, `declaredHookCondition(meta)`. This is the one reading of "this hook has a condition gate". Both `wrapDeclarativeHook` (which installs the gate) and the predicate use it, so the door cannot count a gate that never exists or miss one that does. It is not exported from the package index, so the public surface does not change. The compile and evaluate block in `wrapDeclarativeHook` is the same code, one nesting level shallower.
- `content/docs/automation/hooks.mdx`. The "After hooks run inside the unit of work" table row now names the conditional hook too. Without this, the row would be wrong after this change. The claimed file surface did not include this file; the report says so.
- A changeset, `minor` for `@objectstack/objectql`, declared BREAKING (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, ADR-0087 not-required, no migration). It names what the new unit refuses for a `log` or `async` hook carrying a `condition`, and the fix. Plus two one-clause corrections of the pending #22782 changeset (see "Deliberate correction").

## Mechanism readings (dispatch section 2)

- **Where the condition is visible.** `hook-binder.ts` passes the same metadata `Hook` object to `wrapDeclarativeHook` and, as `meta`, to `registerHook`. So `entry.meta.condition` is exactly what the gate reads, and no new field on the entry is needed. Hooks registered in code have no `meta` and declare no condition. The builtin audit stamps that `plugin.ts` wraps are `before*` only and carry no condition.
- **`async: true`.** The condition gate is step 1 of the wrapper and runs synchronously, before step 2 (fire-and-forget). So an `async: true` hook whose condition cannot be evaluated refuses the write. Before the fix, the async unit pin was red with the row stored. So async hooks are in the predicate.
- **Predicate text** at `63739521d8` matched the dispatch's reading.

## Pins

Unit tests in `packages/objectql/src/engine-after-hook-abort-unit.test.ts`, in a new describe block beside the #22782 one:
- `onError: 'log'` with a condition that cannot be evaluated (`previous` on an insert): refused with `HookConditionError` (`reason: 'unevaluable'`, the hook and event named). The row and the chain's `ctx.api` note are absent, and one unit was begun and rolled back.
- `onError: 'log'` on `afterUpdate` and `afterDelete` (a key the object does not declare): the stored row is what it was before each refused write.
- `async: true` with a condition that cannot be evaluated: refused, the row absent, the handler never ran.
- CONTROL, `log` with a condition that evaluates: the handler throws, `[hook] handler failed (onError=log; suppressing)` is logged, both rows are stored and nothing is rolled back. A `false` condition skips the hook.
- CONTROL, an `abort` hook with the same unbindable condition: refused, the row absent, as #22782 leaves it.
- CONTROL, `skipAutomations`: no unit, the row stored.

The first draft of the first pin kept `noteWriter`, an `abort` hook, which opens the unit by itself. So that pin passed before the fix. The pre-fix run caught this, and the chain writer in this block is now `onError: 'log'`.

Real door: `packages/qa/dogfood/test/hook-after-condition-rollback.dogfood.test.ts`. This is a test-only file, because `objectql` has no real driver in its dev dependencies. It drives REST `POST /data/:object` on the verify stack and reads back through the engine:
- `log` with a condition that cannot be evaluated: `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`, the row absent.
- `async: true` with a condition that cannot be evaluated: `500`, the row absent.
- CONTROL, `log` with a condition that evaluates and a handler that throws: `201`, the row stored.
- CONTROL, `abort` with the same unbindable condition: `500`, the row absent.
- CONTROL, `async: true` with a condition that evaluates: the late `ctx.api` write after 40 ms still lands. A conditional async hook now starts inside the door's unit, so this measures the closed-handle reading from PR #22894 on the new population.

## Ablation (committed fix, then the guard reverted)

The fix was committed before the ablation. `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` reverted the predicate to the pre-fix expression. The tool reported anchor 1 to 0, blob `669d4e7c0dd0` to `8f11826b4054`. Then `@objectstack/objectql` was rebuilt, because dogfood reads `dist/` (`KNOWN_UNALIASED_TEST_IMPORTS`).
- Before mutating, `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` (present mode) found the marker `declaredHookCondition(entry.meta)` in 4 built files, with the tree clean.
- Mutate leg: preflight `--absent` with `--source-marker` passed, with the marker absent from all 14 built files.
  - Unit tests: 3 failed and 11 passed. The red ones are the three new pins (`log` insert, `log` update and delete, `async`), with the row stored or deleted. Every control stayed green.
  - Dogfood: 2 failed and 3 passed. The red ones are the `log` and `async` pins, `expected 1 to be +0` (row stored). All three controls stayed green.
- Restore: `git checkout HEAD`, blob back to `669d4e7c0dd0` (equal to HEAD), and `git diff HEAD` empty. After the rebuild, present-mode preflight found the marker in 4 built files with the tree clean, and dogfood passed 5 of 5.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql test`: 401 files and 7823 tests passed, on `a20ce84865` (this diff without the merge and the doc row).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck` (tsc and `check:test-typecheck`): exit 0.
- Dogfood: the new file and its sibling `hook-after-abort-rollback.dogfood.test.ts` passed 11 of 11. A narrowed `tsc --noEmit` over those two files alone, using the package's tsconfig, exited 0 with both files listed (`--listFiles`). The package's full `tsc` reads `dist/` types of packages not built in this worktree, so it was not run.
- Gates: `dispatch-gates --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 97 commands on this diff. All 97 were run on head `9eb65e6a44`. 96 exited 0. `check-empty-changeset` exited 1 by design: it refuses exactly the deliberately corrected `.changeset/22782-objectql-after-hook-abort-rolls-back.md` (see "Deliberate correction"). `--ran` reconciliation: 97 derived, 97 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN. `check-adr-0087-registration` reads the 22856 note as `[BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing]  not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, and `check-changeset-no-major` reports no `major` bump. Earlier, the same 97 ran on `9ba561108f` (all exit 0) and on `48b64091df` (96 exit 0, `check-empty-changeset` exit 1 by design). An earlier run of the 72 dispatch-time commands on `a20ce84865` had `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` at `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (exit 3, packages not built). On the later heads it measured: 107 entry points in 66 packages load.
- Lint, narrowed: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 4 changed TS files gave 4 files, 0 errors and 0 warnings. 0 warnings also means none of the 4 is ignored by the config. `eslint.config.mjs` enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, no `projectService`), so this diff cannot change the verdict on any untouched file. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.
- objectql source is identical between `a20ce84865` and the final head. Since then the branch gained only the `origin/main` merge (`3f694715ee`, a spec migration text and its changeset), the docs row, and four changeset commits from the patch rounds (`4a3e842580`, `48b64091df`, `b2eefbd375`, `9eb65e6a44`).

## Reach and cost

One transaction per write on an object that carries such a hook, the same cost as #22782's unit. Measured over `examples/` and non-test `packages/**/src`, the real configurations in this population are two showcase `afterUpdate` hooks: `showcase_audit_task_completion` (`showcase_task`) and `showcase_warn_over_budget` (`showcase_project`). Both are `async: true, onError: 'log'` with a condition, and both only log. Updates to those two objects now run in a unit. The over-budget hook's own comment notes that `null > null` would abort its expression, which is this card's case.

## Deliberate correction

This PR changes `.changeset/22782-objectql-after-hook-abort-rolls-back.md`, a pending release note it did not add, in two commits. Each touches only that file and one line of it. After this PR the write door opens its unit for an `onError: 'log'` or `async: true` hook that carries a `condition`, because a condition that cannot be evaluated aborts the write. Two clauses of that note said otherwise:

- `4a3e842580`, the "Unchanged" bullet. It said that no unit is opened for an `onError: 'log'` hook or an `async: true` hook. It now reads "No unit is opened for an `onError: 'log'` or `async: true` hook that carries no `condition` (#22856), …".
- `b2eefbd375`, the remedy at the end of the "Inside the new unit, the rules of any unit apply" bullet. It said "mark the hook `onError: 'log'` or `async: true`, or keep the objects on one datasource". It now reads "mark the hook `onError: 'log'` or `async: true` and give it no `condition` (#22856), or keep the objects on one datasource".

Every other byte of the file is unchanged. Restoring the file from the base would ship two sentences that are false after this PR. `check-empty-changeset` refuses this change by design (its DELIBERATE CORRECTION class), and that red is expected until the correction is confirmed. In this PR's own changeset, commit `48b64091df` drops the sentence that pointed at the old 22782 line, and `9eb65e6a44` declares the change a narrowing and names what the new unit refuses.

## Acceptance notes

- **Triage's third option** (refusing at load time a condition that can never bind on its event) is not folded in. Measured population: 0 hooks in `examples/`, non-test `packages/**/src` and `skills/` carry a condition that can never bind on one of their events. The showcase transition conditions read `previous` on update events only. So nothing to file.
- **The pending #22782 changeset** said no unit opens for an `onError: 'log'` hook or an `async: true` hook, and gave "mark the hook `onError: 'log'` or `async: true`" as the remedy for the rules inside the unit. After this PR both hold only for such a hook with no `condition`, so this PR corrects both clauses (see "Deliberate correction" above).
- **The sanitised `500`** (rather than a `4xx` naming the hook and key) is unchanged. Triage put it in the class of #22764.
- **An `ast`-only condition envelope** gets no gate (`declaredHookCondition` returns nothing). This is pre-existing behaviour, kept byte-identical. `HookSchema` refuses that envelope at authoring. This is a read-only observation, not measured on a public door. Carrier: none.
